pages.text: A mass M at distance D_l bends the light of a star behind it (at 8 kpc) into a ring of angular radius θ_E = √(4GM/c² · D_ls/D_lD_s). A star a distance u Einstein radii off the line is magnified A = (u² + 2)/(u√(u² + 4)). The aim jitters by 0.3 milliarcseconds, so a small, distant lens - a small θ_E - cannot be aimed closely. Starlight only: at night, under open sky.
$(thing)Set$(): Lens mass, Lens distance, Alignment.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Pointing jitter: ±0.3 mas·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): No starlight to focus: it is daytime; Its lenses cannot see the sky.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power follows the magnification.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Einstein radius: θ_E = √(4GM D_ls/(c² D_l D_s))$(br)Effective alignment: u ⊕ jitter/θ_E$(br)Magnification: A = (u² + 2)/(u√(u² + 4))
